name: stream-bridging
context: Data is produced outside the streaming platform — a REST endpoint, a relational table exposed through change data capture, a legacy broker, a file drop, an edge gateway — and must enter the topic bus without the producer taking a build-time or runtime dependency on the streaming stack. The bridge is the component that sits between the foreign source and the binder: it accepts the foreign payload, applies the platform's content-type, partitioning and serialization contract, and publishes it to a destination that may not be known until the first message arrives.
benefits: Foreign producers stay decoupled — a REST controller or a database does not acquire a Kafka client, partitioner or schema dependency
Dynamic destinations let a bridge publish to a target chosen per message, so routing decisions can be made in the producing code
Buffering and reconnection live in one place, so an unavailable broker or a flapping network does not surface in the producer
Change-data-capture bridges bring an entire legacy database into the stream as a changelog without rewriting a single producer
Cross-broker bridging (consume from one messaging system, produce to another) becomes a configuration change rather than an integration project
tradeoffs: Every bridged record pays an extra hop plus a serialization round trip through the platform's contract
Dynamic destination creation is convenient and dangerous: a typo becomes a new topic, and wrong-type messages land as poison records
Exactly-once is not free across a bridge — it requires the sink connector to participate in the transaction, and most legacy sinks cannot
Send-by-default semantics mean a foreign producer can emit whether or not anyone is consuming, turning a bug into unbounded growth
A bridge that transforms is indistinguishable from a filter, and the temptation to put business logic there destroys debuggability
use_cases: A Spring MVC endpoint publishing domain events onto Kafka through a stream bridge without Kafka-specific code
Change data capture streaming a legacy operational database into the platform as a compacted changelog
An edge gateway accepting MQTT from constrained devices and republishing into the central broker
File and object-storage drops (batch) republished as records so batch consumers can join against the live stream
Cross-broker bridging where one application consumes from one messaging system and produces to another
avoid_when: The producer can reasonably depend on the messaging library directly — the bridge only adds indirection
The bridging step needs to aggregate, join or hold state across records
The system requires end-to-end exactly-once through a destination that cannot join the transaction
Traffic is high enough that the bridge's own buffer becomes the backpressure bottleneck
component_types: Foreign source adapter: the non-stream producer (controller, JDBC writer, file watcher, edge agent)
Bridge component: submits data to an output binding while preserving partitioning and content-type semantics
Dynamic destination resolver: creates and caches bindings and destinations on first use
Connector: source or sink connector managing offsets, schema and delivery guarantees
Local buffer: queue absorbing broker unavailability and reconnection storms
Schema registry integration: keeps bridged records on the platform's schema contract
anti_patterns: Putting transformation or business logic inside the bridge instead of in a downstream filter
Publishing per request with no buffer, so a broker hiccup becomes a user-visible error
Creating a new dynamic destination per call instead of reusing the cached binding
Bridging into a non-compacted destination with at-least-once semantics and no idempotent sink
Bridging bidirectionally between two systems without loop detection
design_principles: Foreign producers must not acquire a dependency on the streaming stack
Preserve the platform's invocation contract — content type, partitioning and serialization — across the bridge
Absorb unavailability in the bridge's buffer, never in the producer's request path
Destinations are cached, not created per call
The bridge carries data, not meaning
best_practices: Pre-create output bindings at startup rather than relying on lazy creation from the first send
Keep the bridge logic to serialise-and-send; anything else is a filter or a pipe stage
Declare the delivery guarantee of every bridged destination explicitly and match sinks that can honour it
Size and monitor the bridge buffer; unbounded buffering converts a downstream outage into an OOM
For change-data-capture bridges, snapshot-then-stream consistently or the snapshot and the changelog will interleave wrongly
references: Spring Cloud Stream, Producing and Consuming Messages — bridging foreign sources, StreamBridge and dynamic destinations, https://docs.spring.io/spring-cloud-stream/reference/spring-cloud-stream/producing-and-consuming-messages.html
Spring Cloud Stream, Application Reference Guide — binders, destination binders and bridge processor, https://docs.spring.io/spring-cloud-stream/docs/current/reference/html/spring-cloud-stream.html
Apache Kafka, Kafka Connect Overview and User Guide, https://kafka.apache.org/43/kafka-connect/overview/
Apache Kafka, Core Concepts — source and sink processors, https://kafka.apache.org/43/streams/core-concepts/
